name: set_num_opts
title: Format a numeric vector in a tibble

origin.description: Store pillar numeric options on a vector and leave its class and storage alone.
origin.usage: set_num_opts(x, ..., sigfig = NULL, digits = NULL, label = NULL, scale = NULL, notation = c("fit", "dec", "sci", "eng", "si"), fixed_exponent = NULL, extra_sigfig = NULL)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector. It is not checked with is.numeric, and it is not passed through as.numeric.

arguments.name: sigfig, digits, label, scale, notation, fixed_exponent, extra_sigfig
arguments.text: The same options as num(). The attribute is formatted the same way.

origin.details: The pillar attribute is the same record num() stores. set_num_opts(c(1, 2), sigfig = 2) formats as pillar_num:2 and stays a double with class numeric. An integer vector stays integer. The abbreviation of that plain vector is dbl or int, because the pillar_num method is not dispatched. Decimal notation and a non-zero fixed exponent use the same Incomatible error. A scale still requires a label.
origin.value: x, with a pillar attribute. The existing class is kept.
origin.example:
show_opts <- function(x) {
  cat(paste(format(x, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(typeof(x), " ", paste(class(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(format(attr(x, "pillar", exact = TRUE)), "\n", sep = "")
}

show_opts(set_num_opts(c(1, 2), sigfig = 2))
cat("\n")
show_opts(set_num_opts(1:2, sigfig = 2))

translation.description: The same attribute. The values and the class stay as they were. A plain list of ints stays ints.
translation.usage: set_num_opts(x, sigfig=None, digits=None, label=None, scale=None, notation=None, fixed_exponent=None, extra_sigfig=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A value or a list. A string is one character element. None as the whole argument is NULL and is rejected.

arguments.name: sigfig, digits, label, scale, notation, fixed_exponent, extra_sigfig
arguments.text: The same options as num(). digits is not checked for being a whole number.

translation.details: The result is a PillarNum. .data is a copy of the input. .classes is numeric for floats, integer for ints, and the previous classes when the input is already a PillarNum. .pillar formats as pillar_num:2 for sigfig 2. .abbr is dbl or int unless the class is already pillar_num, in which case it uses the pillar_num abbreviation. num() calls this and then sets class pillar_num.
translation.value: A PillarNum. .pillar is the formatted attribute.
translation.example:
from pillar.num import set_num_opts

def show_opts(value):
    bits = [str(item) if isinstance(item, int) else format(item, "g") for item in value.data]
    print(" ".join(bits))
    print(value.typeof, " ".join(value.classes))
    print(value.pillar)

show_opts(set_num_opts([1.0, 2.0], sigfig=2))
print()
show_opts(set_num_opts([1, 2], sigfig=2))
